title.en: Hedging Language (This may indicate …, It appears that …, tend to)
title.es: El lenguaje atenuado (This may indicate …, It appears that …, tend to)

text.en: Hedging signals that something is not completely certain or not true for everyone. It is common in academic, professional and polite language: “This may indicate a problem.” “Young people tend to use phones more.” Its tools are modal verbs (may, might, could), verbs (seem, appear, tend, suggest), adverbs (probably, arguably, generally) and structures (it is likely that, to some extent). The Spanish “podría”, “parece que”, “tiende a” and “es probable que” match them.
text.es: El lenguaje atenuado (hedging) indica que algo no es del todo seguro o no vale para todos. Es común en el lenguaje académico, profesional y cortés: «This may indicate a problem.» «Young people tend to use phones more.» Sus herramientas son los verbos modales (may, might, could), los verbos (seem, appear, tend, suggest), los adverbios (probably, arguably, generally) y las estructuras (it is likely that, to some extent). El «podría», el «parece que», el «tiende a» y el «es probable que» del español les corresponden.

rows: se podría argumentar (it could be ___ that)

text.en: May, might and could mark a possibility, not a certainty. Will and must express certainty, so they are rarer in careful text: “This may be due to stress.” “It could suggest a problem.”
text.es: May, might y could marcan una posibilidad, no una certeza. Will y must expresan certeza, por eso son más raros en un texto cuidadoso: «This may be due to stress.» «It could suggest a problem.»

title.en: Hedging verbs: seem, appear, tend, suggest, indicate
title.es: Verbos atenuantes: seem, appear, tend, suggest, indicate

text.en: After seem and appear comes a to-infinitive or a that-clause. Tend to means a general tendency. Suggest and indicate are weaker than prove: “The results suggest that the method works.”
text.es: Después de seem y appear va un to-infinitivo o una cláusula con that. Tend to significa una tendencia general. Suggest e indicate son más débiles que prove: «The results suggest that the method works.»

tr.en: Young people tend to use phones more.
tr.es: Los jóvenes tienden a usar más el celular.

text.en: An impersonal form: “It appears that prices will rise.” “The drug seems to be effective.”
text.es: Una forma impersonal: «It appears that prices will rise.» «The drug seems to be effective.»

text.en: Probably, possibly, arguably, apparently, generally, relatively, somewhat; to some extent, in most cases, to a certain degree. Instead of the absolute “always, never, all” you often use “often, rarely, most”.
text.es: Probably, possibly, arguably, apparently, generally, relatively, somewhat; to some extent, in most cases, to a certain degree. En lugar de los absolutos «always, never, all» se usa a menudo «often, rarely, most».

tr.en: Arguably, the situation has improved.
tr.es: Podría decirse que la situación ha mejorado.

text.en: It is likely / possible / probable that…; there is some evidence that…; it could be argued that… For requests: “I was wondering if you could help me.” “It might be better to wait.”
text.es: It is likely / possible / probable that…; there is some evidence that…; it could be argued that… Para peticiones: «I was wondering if you could help me.» «It might be better to wait.»

tr.en: It is likely that the economy will recover.

tr.en: I was wondering if you could help me.

text.en: Hedging is not weakness but accuracy: if something is not certain, will or always is too strong. Too many hedges, however, make the text vague: one or two per sentence are enough.
text.es: El lenguaje atenuado no es debilidad sino exactitud: si algo no es seguro, will o always es demasiado fuerte. Demasiados atenuantes, en cambio, vuelven vago el texto: basta uno o dos por oración.

text.en: Spanish influence: the Spanish “puede ser que” is it may be that in English, and “a lo mejor” is perhaps. The Spanish “tiende a” is tends to, and with a plural subject tend to: “Young people tend to…”.
text.es: Influencia del español: el «puede ser que» del español es it may be that en inglés, y «a lo mejor» es perhaps. El «tiende a» es tends to, y con sujeto plural tend to: «Young people tend to…».

speak.en: Hedging signals that something is not completely certain or not true for everyone. Its tools are «may», «might» and «could»: «This may indicate a problem». The verbs are «seem», «appear», «tend», «suggest»: «The results suggest that the method works», «Young people tend to use phones more». The structures are «it is likely that», «to some extent», «in most cases». For a polite request: «I was wondering if you could help me».
speak.es: El lenguaje atenuado indica que algo no es del todo seguro o no vale para todos. Sus herramientas son «may», «might» y «could»: «This may indicate a problem». Los verbos son «seem», «appear», «tend», «suggest»: «The results suggest that the method works», «Young people tend to use phones more». Las estructuras son «it is likely that», «to some extent», «in most cases». Para una petición cortés: «I was wondering if you could help me».

why.en: May marks a careful possibility: this may be.
why.es: May marca una posibilidad cautelosa: this may be.

may to.en: After may there is no to; the base verb follows.
may to.es: Después de may no va to; sigue el verbo base.

maybe.en: Maybe is an adverb (“perhaps”); the modal verb here is two words (may be).
maybe.es: Maybe es un adverbio («quizá»); el verbo modal aquí es de dos palabras (may be).

tr.en: This may be caused by stress.
tr.es: Esto puede ser causado por el estrés.

why.es: Un sujeto plural: the results suggest.

suggests.en: Suggests is singular; results is plural.
suggests.es: Suggests es singular; results es plural.

suggesting.en: Suggesting is not a finite verb; you need a finite form.
suggesting.es: Suggesting no es un verbo conjugado; hace falta una forma conjugada.

why.en: An impersonal hedge: it appears that.
why.es: Un atenuante impersonal: it appears that.

appear.en: “It appear” is not correct; it is singular, so you need appears.
appear.es: «It appear» no es correcto; it es singular, por eso hace falta appears.

appearing.en: “It appearing” is not a finite verb; you need a finite form.
appearing.es: «It appearing» no es un verbo conjugado; hace falta una forma conjugada.

why.es: Un sujeto plural: young people tend to.

tends.en: Tends is singular; young people is plural.
tends.es: Tends es singular; young people es plural.

tending.en: Tending is not a finite verb; you need a finite form.
tending.es: Tending no es un verbo conjugado; hace falta una forma conjugada.

items.sentence: To some ___, the plan has worked.

why.en: A fixed phrase: to some extent.
why.es: Una expresión fija: to some extent.

extends.en: Extends is a verb; the phrase needs a noun (extent).
extends.es: Extends es un verbo; la expresión necesita un sustantivo (extent).

extend.en: Extend is a verb; the phrase needs a noun (extent).
extend.es: Extend es un verbo; la expresión necesita un sustantivo (extent).

examples: To some extent, he is right.
To a large extent, it works.

tr.es: Hasta cierto punto, el plan ha funcionado.

items.sentence: It is ___ that the economy will recover.

like.en: “It is like that” has another meaning (“it is like that”); you need likely.
like.es: «It is like that» tiene otro significado («es así»); hace falta likely.

liked.en: “It is liked that” is not correct; you need likely.
liked.es: «It is liked that» no es correcto; hace falta likely.

examples: It is likely that he knows.

tr.en: It is likely that the economy will recover.
tr.es: Es probable que la economía se recupere.

items.sentence: It could be ___ that the policy failed.

why.en: A passive structure: it could be argued that.
why.es: Una estructura pasiva: it could be argued that.

argue.en: After be you need a participle (argued), not the base verb.
argue.es: Después de be hace falta un participio (argued), no el verbo base.

arguing.en: “Could be arguing” would be a continuous active form; the structure is passive (argued).
arguing.es: «Could be arguing» sería una forma activa continua; la estructura es pasiva (argued).

examples: It could be said that he lied.
It may be argued that it works.

tr.en: It could be argued that the policy failed.
tr.es: Se podría argumentar que la política falló.

seems.en: Seems is singular; results is plural.

Argue.en: Argue is a base verb; you need a sentence-opening adverb (Arguably).

items.sentence: I was ___ if you could help me.

why.en: A careful suggestion: it might be better to.
why.es: Una sugerencia cautelosa: it might be better to.

more good.en: “More good” is not correct; the comparative of good is better.
more good.es: «More good» no es correcto; el comparativo de good es better.

well.en: Well is an adverb; after be you need an adjective (better).
well.es: Well es un adverbio; después de be hace falta un adjetivo (better).

It might be easier to ask.
